text.p: Xechem International Inc said on Tuesday that the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office issued Xechem a patent for a method for the isolation and purification from raw organic matter containing paclitaxel, cephalomannine and other related taxanes.
Paclitaxel, a well known anticancer pharmaceutical for an array of cancer tumor cells, is primarily extracted from the bark of the Pacific Yew tree, Xechem said.
Because the concentration of paclitaxel in raw materials is low, extraction had previously required expensive commercial isolation or semi-synthesis, Xechem said.
Xechem's patented method now permits isolation of paclitaxel from crude biomass containing a complex mixture of taxane-type compounds in high yield, it said. A taxane is an anti-cancer agent.
